record.original_question: Let lambda_n(s) be the canonically indexed eigenvalues of the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator for the Gauss continued-fraction map, indexed so that the labeling by n is canonical and corresponds to ordering by magnitude. For each nontrivial zero rho of the Riemann zeta function, let t(rho) be the integer M such that lambda_M(rho/2) = 1. Given a fixed integer M in N, determine what can be said about the set t^(-1)(M): whether it is infinite, how the conjectural distribution of Riemann zeros changes when restricted to that set, and how one can compute sets such as t^(-1)(1) effectively.

evidence.quote: In particular, for each nontrivial zero rho of the Riemann zeta function there exist an integer M = t(rho) such that lambda_M(rho/2) = 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T:[0,1]\to[0,1] be the Gauss continued-fraction map T(x)=1/x-\lfloor 1/x\rfloor (with T(0)=0). For a complex parameter s with \mathrm{Re}\,s>1/2, the Mayer–Ruelle transfer operator \mathcal{L}_s is defined on a suitable Banach space of holomorphic functions on a disk containing [0,1] by
\[
(\mathcal{L}_s f)(z)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(k+z)^{2s}}\, f\!\left(\frac{1}{k+z}\right).
\]
For each such s, \mathcal{L}_s is nuclear and has a discrete spectrum of eigenvalues which can be canonically indexed as a sequence \{\lambda_n(s)\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} (for instance, in non-increasing order of magnitude, with the canonical labeling extended analytically in s).

It is known that for every nontrivial zero \rho of the Riemann zeta function \zeta there exists a unique positive integer M=t(\rho)\in\mathbb{N} such that
\[
\lambda_{M}\!\left(\tfrac{\rho}{2}\right)=1.
\]
This defines a map t from the set of nontrivial zeros of \zeta to \mathbb{N}.

Fix M\in\mathbb{N}. Address the following:

(a) Is the fiber t^{-1}(M)=\{\rho:\zeta(\rho)=0,\ 0<\mathrm{Re}\,\rho<1,\ t(\rho)=M\} infinite?

(b) Assuming the Riemann hypothesis and the standard conjectural distribution of nontrivial zeros (e.g.\ the Montgomery pair-correlation / GUE distribution of normalized spacings), how does the distribution of zeros change when one restricts to the subset t^{-1}(M)?

(c) Provide an effective procedure to compute the set t^{-1}(1) (the nontrivial zeros \rho for which \rho/2 is a parameter at which the largest canonical eigenvalue of \mathcal{L}_s equals 1).
artifact.status_search_result: The relationship between zeros of 1-\lambda_n(s) for the Mayer transfer operator and the nontrivial zeros of \zeta is established (Mayer; Lewis–Zagier; recent asymptotic results), but no published work resolves the fiber structure of the index map t, the conditional distribution of zeros within fibers t^{-1}(M), or gives an effective algorithm for t^{-1}(1). The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Transfer operator for the Gauss' continued fraction map. I. Structure of the eigenvalues and trace formulas
status_evidence.snippet: Every factor 1-λ_n(s) vanishes at (halves of) some Riemann zeros and spectral parameters of even Maass forms; every factor 1+λ_n(s) vanishes at corresponding odd objects.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the link between eigenvalues of the Mayer transfer operator and Riemann zeros, but does not resolve the fiber/distribution questions on t^{-1}(M).

status_evidence.title: On the Ruelle-Mayer Transfer Operators for Hölder Continuous Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent asymptotics for eigenvalues of the Mayer transfer operator settling conjectures of Mayer-Roepstorff, MacLeod, Flajolet-Vallée.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work refines spectral asymptotics but does not address the fiber problem for t.
